```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../setup.R")
docs_setup(legend = "right", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
```

An ordination places observations on a small set of axes computed from their measured variables. A biplot draws the observations and variable directions in the same view. `biplot_3d()` composes site points, solid-headed quiver arrows and optional group regions.

The examples use iris measurements to draw principal-component scores, match
groups by identifier and display ecological ordination scores. Installation
is covered in [Get started](ggplot3d.html); the final example also requires vegan.

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
```

```{r iris, fig.alt="Iris flowers on three principal-component axes, with measurement arrows and ellipsoids describing the species groups."}
fit <- prcomp(iris[1:4], scale. = TRUE)
groups <- setNames(iris$Species, rownames(iris))
ggplot() + biplot_3d(fit, groups = groups, region = "ellipsoid",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

For `prcomp`, sites use `fit$x` and arrows use `fit$rotation`. `loading_scale` explicitly multiplies the arrow vectors for display. The chosen multiplier therefore belongs in a figure's methods or caption. `choices` selects the three axes.

Site identifiers are the score matrix's row names, or sequential character identifiers when row names are absent. Group membership is joined by these identifiers. A named vector or a table with `id` and `group` columns can supply membership in any order.

```{r hull, fig.alt="The iris principal-component scores with a convex hull around each species, using group membership joined by identifier."}
membership <- data.frame(id = names(groups), group = unname(groups))
membership <- membership[rev(seq_len(nrow(membership))), ]
ggplot() + biplot_3d(fit, groups = membership, region = "hull",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

## Vegan scores

[vegan](https://vegandevs.github.io/vegan/) supplies ecological ordination methods and a `scores()` generic that applies their scaling conventions. `biplot_3d()` calls that generic for vegan fits. Pass method-specific arguments in `scores_args`, or supply a list containing `sites` and `species` score matrices directly.

```{r vegan, eval=requireNamespace("vegan", quietly=TRUE), fig.alt="An iris ordination from vegan with species groups and labelled variable arrows."}
model <- vegan::rda(iris[1:4], scale = TRUE)
ggplot() + biplot_3d(model, groups = groups,
                        scores_args = list(scaling = 2), label_size = 5) + coord_3d(clip = "off")
```

The species arrows of this fit reach the edge of the box. `clip = "off"` lets their labels extend past the drawing area of the panel instead of being cut at its edge.

The group ellipsoids use `stat_ellipsoid_3d(type = "norm")`. Their level describes the spread of observations under that covariance model. Individual point, quiver, text, hull and ellipsoid layers can also be composed directly when a figure needs separate mappings. [vegan3d](https://rdrr.io/cran/vegan3d/man/vegan3d-package.html) documents the corresponding ordination and group-region conventions.
